newsitem.title: USA: IGG gets immunotherapeutic agent patent.
newsitem.headline: IGG gets immunotherapeutic agent patent.

text.p: IGG Inc said that the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office has issued a patent covering the company's immunotherapeutic agent, MMS-1, as well as the company's methods of preparing the compound.

MMS-1 is a carbohydrate-based agent derived from bacterial cells that has been shown in animal models to enhance immune system activity, particularly in the treatment of cancer and immunosuppressive viral infections, it said.

"It has long been known that some bacteria manifest strong immunostimulatory and anti-tumor activities," said David Platt, chief executive officer in a press release. "The therapeutic potential of these bacteria, however, has been limited by their associated toxicity."

The company said that MMS-1 is a purified carbohydrate based component derived from bacteria that has shown in animal studies to inhibit metastasis and reduce primary tumors without exhibiting the toxicity commonly associated with whole bacteria.
